title: Autumn partner sea level gave no clear winter forecast gain at San Francisco and Seattle in 1991-2025
abstract: We tested whether autumn mean sea level at the other Pacific gauge improves winter forecasts after local autumn level, a linear time trend, and autumn Nino 3.4 are known. We used fixed NOAA sources for San Francisco and Seattle. Each winter fit used earlier complete winters only. Common support gave 33 test winters in 1991-2025. The equal mean reduction in mean squared error was 3.97%, with a conditional 95% five-year block interval of -2.77% to 9.54%. Site estimates were 7.53% at San Francisco and 0.41% at Seattle; both intervals included zero. All planned sensitivity intervals also included zero. The result leaves added partner value uncertain for this model and season. It does not prove that spatial ocean data lack value. Retrospective sources, selected sites, missing months, short records, and uncertainty conditional on fitted histories limit inference. The package includes exact source hashes, used monthly fields, all forecasts, code, uncertainty draws, two figures, a numerical audit, and a successful offline repeat. It does not predict flood events or identify a physical cause.
